chunks: If We give him a taste of Our favour after some distress he has known, he says: 'It was my due. I cannot imagine the Hour will come. And even if I go back to my Lord, there will surely still be the best for me with Him.' We shall tell those who do not believe what they used to do, and inflict on them a heavy punishment.
ai.seo_question: What does the arrogant person say when relief comes after hardship, and what is God's response?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological shift of the arrogant disbeliever who, upon relief from hardship, attributes divine favor to his own merit and becomes complacent about the Day of Judgment. This self-deception leads to a severe reckoning, where God exposes the truth of their deeds and inflicts a heavy punishment, serving as a warning against spiritual arrogance during times of ease.
